g.title: kll_technique
g.text: 4 execs × 4 cores = 16 parallel tasks · bounded RANGE frame · symmetric halo (PRECEDING + FOLLOWING) · client concat

g.title: cluster_s1
g.text: · per-executor, streaming (KLL dam-break, no sort, halo-oblivious)

g.title: cluster_s2
g.text: · 16 parallel Ballista tasks · full window per range, halo labelled at pull time

g.title: scheduler
g.text: · invariant: ties on v2 stay together
· bin-packer may split sub-parts (must, on overlap); tolerates heterogeneous k_i
emit assignment (pull-list, keep_range=[g_i, g_{i+1})) per partition-id 0..15

g.title: client
g.text: pulls partition-ids 0..15 in order, serial flatten → 1 sorted stream

g.title: legend
g.text: Halo mechanism (bounded RANGE frame, numeric ORDER BY)
· halo_lo = WindowFrame's PRECEDING extent in value units (e.g. 3 for RANGE 3 PRECEDING)
· halo_hi = WindowFrame's FOLLOWING extent in value units (0 if frame ends at CURRENT ROW)
· Stage 1's RangeRepart stays halo-oblivious — sub-parts locally disjoint, no dup rows
· scheduler math: task i's fetch range = [g_i - halo_lo, g_{i+1} + halo_hi]
· BWAG sees halo rows on both sides and includes them in frames of real rows
· HaloDropExec keeps only v2 ∈ [g_i, g_{i+1}) after BWAG — halo rows vanish
· edges: g_0 = -∞ (no low halo needed), g_16 = +∞ (no high halo needed); planner elides
· RANGE N PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW (halo_lo=N, halo_hi=0)
· RANGE CURRENT ROW AND M FOLLOWING (halo_lo=0, halo_hi=M)
· RANGE N PRECEDING AND M FOLLOWING (halo_lo=N, halo_hi=M)
· NOT covered: UNBOUNDED PRECEDING / FOLLOWING (halo would span the world; needs
two-pass running-agg propagation instead — separate technique)
Why HaloDropExec is a custom op, not a FilterExec + __is_halo column
· DF's PushDownFilter would chase a standard filter downward through Sort/SPM/BWAG
· pushdown is bounded only by the column-adding projection — putting that projection
below BWAG lets pushdown drop halo rows BEFORE they feed frames (silent corruption)
· custom physical ops are invisible to the standard pushdown rules — optimizer walks over
· no schema growth, no projection dance, no correctness footgun
Why this doesn't cover non-continuous ORDER BY (strings, etc.)
· SQL only permits RANGE frames on numeric/datetime/interval types
· string ORDER BY forces ROWS frames — halo becomes row-count-based, needs
Stage 1 to emit sub-part row counts and scheduler to bin-pack on cumulative rank
· ROWS-frame follow-up; deferred, not blocking the RANGE ship
· execution_stage.rs:1089 emits partitions in id order
· partition 0 fully drains before partition 1 → global sort by construction
· target = 16 range partitions (partition-id i owns [g_i, g_{i+1}) output)
· half-open [g_i, g_{i+1}) is the tie-handling convention — all v2 == g_i go to partition i
· splits sub-parts freely (overlap forces it anyway)
· halo_lo/halo_hi must be < partition width, else pull spans >1 neighbor and read amp blows up
Plan-time fallbacks to naive single-partition BWAG plan
· halo_span > partition_width × threshold (e.g. 0.5) → don't halo >50% of the data
· single v2 value's frequency > 1/target_partitions → hot-value skew, can't bin-pack around it
· partition_width and frequency estimated from parquet column stats at plan time
Dynamic k (each exec picks its own k_i at dam-break)
· k_min = ceil(target_partitions × oversample / n_execs) — bin-pack flexibility floor
· k_max ≈ KLL_internal_K / margin (~25-50 for default K=200) — sketch resolution ceiling
· at dam-break, exec knows exact local row count (parquet), extrapolated byte size, and
real distribution (KLL) — enough to make an informed local decision
· bin-packer at scheduler tolerates heterogeneous k_i: dense execs emit more, sparse fewer
· this is how the design absorbs skew: hot slices split themselves before shuffle-write
Why oversampling matters at all (whichever k formula)
· k too small → bin-packer has no degrees of freedom → skew propagates into Stage 2
· k too small → wide local sub-parts → large cross-exec overlap → HaloDrop reads amplify
· k too small → KLL boundary error (~1/k) can't distinguish target cuts
· k too large → sub-parts < 50-100 MB → shuffle metadata overhead dominates
· practical range for h2o (10 GB): 64-160 sub-parts total (16-40 per exec)
